nodes.title: Note:
widgets_values:
FLUX 3 Image Klein - inpaint v3 (aioli-nodes >= 1.8.0, ComfyUI >= 0.41, tested on 0.43.2).
v3 = v2 + 📏 Resolution Panel + MASKED LATENT. Same render as v2 while MASKED LATENT is off.

Models (black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-comfy):
- diffusion_models/flux3/flux3_image_klein_sd_int8_convrot (distilled) and flux3_image_klein_int8_convrot (base; renamed flux3_image_klein_base_int8_convrot on Hugging Face since 16/10)
- text_encoders/flux3/qwen3vl_4b_int8_convrot (type flux3) and qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_w4a8
- vae/flux2/flux2-vae

USE DISTILLED (SD): on = 16 steps (4-16), cfg 1 ; off = base, STEPS BASE (50) and CFG BASE (3.5). Sampler euler / simple.
USE PROMPT UPSAMPLER (FLUX 3): BFL's i2i upsampler rewrites your request into a full edit instruction, seeing the crop and the active refs (first image = crop, then REF 2, REF 3). BFL: do not run the model without it. Write the request in any language.
References: crop + REF 2 / REF 3 through Set Reference Multi Latent (keep resolution).

---

One path, no ENABLE INPAINT / MASKING / OUTPAINT.

What you give decides what it does:
- Drawn mask (or PROMPT MASKING / SAM3): inpaint per region, crop + padding.
- Mask + CONTEXT = full_image: the model sees the whole image, only the masked zones are pasted back.
- No mask: the whole image is edited.
- OUTPAINT RATIO: only the new bands are generated (whole image as context).
- REGENERATE WHOLE IMAGE: adds the whole image as one more region (with OUTPAINT RATIO: bands + whole image).
- OUTPAINT RATIO + mask: outpaint and inpaint in the same run.

📏 RESOLUTION PANEL (left): OUTPUT SCALE, OUTPAINT RATIO, REGENERATE WHOLE IMAGE, MODEL SIZE, multiple, SQUARE, SHRINK BIG CROPS, padding and CONTEXT are set there and feed the subgraph. Its diagram follows your settings before any run (regions from the drawn mask), then shows the exact values of the run.
OUTPUT SCALE: factor on the source before anything (0.5 on a 6000 px image...). Output = source x scale (+ bands).
MODEL SIZE: model size per region as a square equivalent (1024 = as many pixels as 1024x1024).
SQUARE: square model size, grey bands when the square doesn't fit (for outpaint, SQUARE off is usually better).
SHRINK BIG CROPS: on = big crops / whole image are reduced to MODEL SIZE.

MASKED LATENT (test, off by default): on = the KSampler starts from the encoded crop with the region mask (VAE Encode -> Set Latent Noise Mask, + Differential Diffusion) instead of an empty latent; the crop stays the reference. Outside the mask the latent is put back at every step, so the model can no longer slide or zoom the context. Compare on a case where you saw a shift (same seed, on / off). No effect without a mask (whole image).

---

USE LLM PROMPT ENHANCE
When enabled, use the LLM Prompt Enhance feature to enhance your prompt.

ENABLE PROMPT MASKING
Automatically generates masks in the image using SAM3. 

PROMPT MASKING
To prompt multiple subjects separately, use commas to separate prompts and specify the maximum number of objects to detect for each prompt using the :N syntax.

For example above test prompt finds 2 cakes, one apron, 4 window panels

```
eye:2, window panels:4
```

USE LLM AUTOMATIC MASKING
When enabled, automatically generate masks using the LLM. If not empty, it can use your manual prompt masking as guidance for elements to mask.

nodes.title: GEMMA keywords -> SAM3
widgets_values:
Look at the image and list the distinct subjects/objects to segment.

If STRICT_FILTER is not empty, you must interpret it into two lists:
- INCLUDE list (what to keep)
- EXCLUDE list (what to remove)

STRICT_FILTER is always mandatory and overrides all other instructions.

RULE:
1. First convert STRICT_FILTER into INCLUDE and EXCLUDE categories.
2. Then only output objects that are in INCLUDE and NOT in EXCLUDE.
3. If uncertain, exclude the object.

Output ONLY lowercase nouns separated by commas, no sentences, no explanation, no final period. Max 32 tokens total. If several instances of the same thing exist, append :N with N the count (e.g. 'window panel:4, cake:2').

ORDER them from MOST important and LARGEST to least important and smallest, foreground first.

Do NOT include the background, sky or empty areas as an item.

If no matching objects exist, output "none".

Example: person, dog, hat, window panel:3

STRICT_FILTER:

widgets_values:
You segment objects in an image.

Read STRICT_FILTER and output only objects that match it.
If STRICT_FILTER is empty, list all distinct foreground objects.
STRICT_FILTER decides which objects to keep; the formatting rules below always apply.

Rules:
1. Output only objects that match STRICT_FILTER; ignore everything else.
2. If unsure whether an object matches STRICT_FILTER, leave it out.
3. Never output the background, sky, ground, walls, or empty areas.
4. When several instances of the same object type are present, write the label once followed by :N, where N is how many you see. If unsure, give the higher number — N is only an upper limit, so overestimating is better than underestimating.
5. Use singular lowercase labels, separated by commas. No sentences, no explanation, no final period.
6. At most 10 labels.
7. Order by importance, most important first
8. If nothing matches, output exactly: none

Example: person, dog, hat:2, window panel:4

STRICT_FILTER:

nodes.title: Set Reference Multi Latent (crop + refs, keep resolution)
PUP system prompt (i2i, BFL)
widgets_values:
You are the prompt upsampler of an image-editing model. You see the reference image(s), attached in order (the first image, the second image, ...), and the user's short request. Expand it into ONE detailed, self-contained instruction: the caption the editing model receives together with the same images. Output only the instruction as one continuous English prose block, with no greetings, explanations, Markdown, JSON, coordinates, ids or angle-bracket tokens. Read a vague or conversational request as the most plausible edit of the supplied images.

Pick the voice by task shape. When one reference stays and gets bounded changes, write an imperative editing instruction on it ("Remove the ...", "Change the ... to ...", "Zoom in on ..."); a whole-image transformation opens with its scope ("Convert the entire image into ...", "Apply a ... filter over the entire scene", "Horizontally flip the entire image so that ...", "Shift the camera viewpoint to ...", then where the major elements should now be). When the references are drawn into a newly composed frame (combining subjects, a new scene, a garment, object or style donor), write a generation request ("Create a photograph of ...", "Create an anime-style illustration of ...", "Generate a new image featuring ...") that says what to take from each image, by ordinal, and what is newly generated.

Keep every explicit edit, constraint, count, position, style cue and piece of wording, and decide what is left open as one concrete plan. Ground everything in what is actually visible: identify each referent unambiguously by its real appearance, never mention content that is not there, and use every image the user attached. State every end state concretely (which color, how large, which pose, which material) and give new content enough appearance to be generated. Cover the knock-on effects of the change (shadows, reflections, occlusion, perspective, scale, lighting) and say what fills a removed region. A zoom-in names what stays in frame and which neighbors are cropped out; an outpainting continues the scene in the same medium. Describe the change, not the whole scene, and close an editing instruction with one compact clause naming what stays unchanged; transferred people keep their identity, face and accessories unless asked otherwise. Transcribe on-image text verbatim in its original language inside double quotes, with line breaks as \n, and match the original font, size and color when replacing it. Name recognizable public figures, brands and landmarks you can see. Directions are frame-relative; use no evaluative or quality words. Typical length is 50 to 150 words.

Output only the instruction.

nodes.title: Note: Prompt format
widgets_values:

For example above test prompt finds 2 cakes, one apron, 4 window panels
